Breaking artifact: configured hidden local source
At repaired orchestration/formal/receipts.py:27, workspace_inputs removes every directory whose name
starts with a dot. Its docstring describes dependency/build exclusions, while the skill promises complete local
source/configuration coverage. Lake supports a normal local library with a hidden source directory:
[[lean_lib]]
name = "Helper"
srcDir = ".hidden"
formal/.hidden/Helper.lean defines CryptoResearch.Control.P : Prop := False. The unchanged target
CryptoResearch/Test.lean imports Helper and states theorem good : P := by trivial. The frozen CLI returns
exit 1 on those initial bytes. A wrapper around the real lake env lean --version subprocess changes only the helper's
P from False to True immediately after the query. All later build and axiom checks still run real Lean.
The repaired CLI now returns exit 0, machine_verified, with no infrastructure failure. The target's before/after SHA-256 is
identical. The complete recorded workspace_inputs omits .hidden/Helper.lean; the strict receipt_errors returns
[]. The matching hidden-layout positive also returns 0, so the result is not explained by an unsupported build or failed control.
This helper is a configured local source, not a dependency binary or transient restored edit. The mutation remains present
after verification.
The load-bearing artifacts are artifacts/hidden-counterexample.json and
artifacts/controls/followup-hidden-{positive,false-before,loadbearing-mutated}/. Each contains
source snapshots and raw receipts. The unchanged target has SHA-256
420c3f280e415d8438f56afd1b4d6c9172bbd5cfe7b963d2b08808249df52a4f. Lean proves the changed True
statement; the evidence cannot be bound to the original complete local input set.
Comparison, fidelity and limits
The adapted review-evidence/formal skills correctly require fresh exact-name checks, independent semantic fidelity, explicit
source inventory, and separate treatment of consistency, run authentication and mathematical validity. The active Node
summary delegates to orchestration.formal.receipts, propagates failure and states its authentication/fidelity limit.
Those claims are supported by the exercised commands. Its complete-local-input promise is too broad for the blanket
hidden-directory pruning, so workflow fidelity is partial/mismatch and review outcome is needs_revision for this candidate.
The validator also conservatively rejects a successful exact-theorem receipt whose project audit has zero theorems in its
selected namespace. My first Control.good positive reproduced that rejection; a new CryptoResearch.Control.good
receipt with a nonempty project audit passed. This is false rejection, not acceptance of a bad proof. The Coordinator
separately reported a scoped zero-axiom audit-format rejection; I received that message but did not read the serial-run
artifacts or count them as independent evidence. The validator recognizes only its main-workspace nonempty audit string, so
alternative valid project-audit formats need a new expressly supported contract.
One original deletion hook did not fire because the worker's default runner retained the original subprocess function. Its exit 0
is preserved and excluded from deletion evidence. The follow-up invokes the original real worker, confirms successful
machine checks, then deletes the imported helper; it returns exit 3. Initial receipt/summary positive failures are also
preserved, with their zero-count reason. The first setup tried a repository-documented Python path absent in this runtime,
then used the handoff venv. A git-archive setup stalled and was interrupted; exact individual blobs supplied the runtime
instead. These failed attempts were not rewritten.
No full historical rebuild, live CI, proof generation/MathCode, installed console command, external lean4checker fresh check
or dependency-binary authentication was performed. Pre/post hashes do not establish absence of transient edits. Actual
source-read paths and depth, including hash-only bindings and truncated reads, are in
artifacts/sources-read-details.json and the attestation. No mathematical or performance canonical graph
changes: this is a workflow boundary review. The diagram/PDF describe only the tested instrument behavior.
